International Business Machines (IBM) has put quantum error correction in the spotlight by launching a co-design platform with Oak Ridge National Laboratory and AMD that tightly links its quantum processors with high performance classical computing.

IBM's recent quantum and AI announcements have landed against a mixed share price backdrop, with the stock at US$247.11 after a 1-month share price return of 11.67%, but a year-to-date share price decline of 15.23% and a 1-year total shareholder return down 18.85%.

International Business Machines looks busy building the future of quantum and AI, yet the share price has fallen this year. Is this still a strong business temporarily on sale, or is the recent rebound already fair value?

Most Popular Narrative: 3.5% Undervalued

International Business Machines is trading at $247.11 while the most followed narrative on the stock pegs fair value closer to $256.08. That gap is small, yet it reflects a view that IBM's mix of quantum, AI and recurring software still is not fully appreciated in the current quote.

IBM represents a defensive growth technology investment transitioning into a software and AI-led enterprise platform company. While topline growth remains moderate, improving mix (software), strong margins, and durable cash flows underpin a compelling long-term investment case, particularly for investors seeking exposure to enterprise AI with lower volatility than pure-play SaaS peers.

title: What Just Happened To Accenture Stock?

What Just Happened To Accenture Stock?
Trefis Team

Accenture (ACN) stock gained 49.9% from May 9 to November 5, 2026, while the S&P 500 slipped 0.08% over the same period. The shares logged their biggest one-day gain of the past year on October 1, climbing 15.8% when Accenture reported its fiscal fourth-quarter 2026 results and gave its outlook for fiscal 2027. What did that report show about the business?

From June's Low To October's Forecast-Beating Report

Accenture posted fiscal fourth-quarter revenue of $18.7 billion, up 7% in local currency. Management said this result topped the high end of its guided range. Clients signed $22.2 billion of new bookings during the quarter. Managed services generated $9.4 billion of the quarter's revenue and booked a record $12.8 billion of new work.

The six-month gain also includes a steep drop. Shares fell 18.0% on June 18, the day of Accenture's fiscal third-quarter earnings call, and closed at their lowest level of the past year on June 30. On that call, management lowered its full-year revenue growth outlook to 3% to 4% in local currency.

Most of the six-month gain came after the October report. From October 7 to November 5, the shares returned 35.9%, while the S&P 500 lost 5.7%. Counting the report day itself, the share price is up 45.8% since the September 30 close. Accenture's peers also rose, though less: Cognizant gained 30% from May 9 to November 5.

The S&P 500's 5.7% slide included a 4.4% drop on November 5. Here's how the market did after 21 days like it.

Accenture Now Trades At Nearly Double June's P/E

At the end of June, Accenture stock traded at 9.8 times its twelve-month earnings, its lowest quarterly reading since fiscal 2017. At the November 5 close, it traded at 19.1 times, still below the S&P 500's 22.9 times.

Accenture's profit grew far less than its share price. Net income for fiscal 2026 was $8.37 billion, against $7.68 billion in fiscal 2025. The share price rise since June therefore comes mostly from a higher price on Accenture's profit, and only a little from a larger profit.

Management Still Expects Growth Near Last Year's Pace

Management expects fiscal 2027 revenue to grow 3% to 6% in local currency, a range centered just below the 5% local-currency growth Accenture posted in fiscal 2026. Reported growth had already eased, with fiscal 2026 revenue rising 6.5% against 7.4% in fiscal 2025. In other words, Accenture's growth is about where it was before its shares rose, or a little slower. At its October 14 Investor Day, though, Accenture outlined a multiyear strategy aimed at faster growth, and some analysts raised their price targets afterward.

Is Most-Watched Stock International Business Machines Corporation (IBM) Worth Betting on Now?
Zacks Equity Research

IBM
^GSPC

Trading disclosure

IBM (IBM) has been one of the most searched-for stocks on Zacks.com lately. So, you might want to look at some of the facts that could shape the stock's performance in the near term.

Over the past month, shares of this technology and consulting company have returned +9.1%, compared to the Zacks S&P 500 composite's -5.4% change. During this period, the Zacks Computer - Integrated Systems industry, which IBM falls in, has lost 34.2%. The key question now is: What could be the stock's future direction?

Although media reports or rumors about a significant change in a company's business prospects usually cause its stock to trend and lead to an immediate price change, there are always certain fundamental factors that ultimately drive the buy-and-hold decision.

Revisions to Earnings Estimates

Rather than focusing on anything else, we at Zacks prioritize evaluating the change in a company's earnings projection. This is because we believe the fair value for its stock is determined by the present value of its future stream of earnings.

We essentially look at how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to reflect the impact of the latest business trends. And if earnings estimates go up for a company, the fair value for its stock goes up. A higher fair value than the current market price drives investors' interest in buying the stock, leading to its price moving higher. This is why empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.

For the current quarter, IBM is expected to post earnings of $4.63 per share, indicating a change of +2.4% from the year-ago quarter. The Zacks Consensus Estimate has changed +0.7% over the last 30 days.

For the current fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $12.41 points to a change of +7.1% from the prior year. Over the last 30 days, this estimate has changed +0.6%.

For the next fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $13.24 indicates a change of +6.7% from what IBM is expected to report a year ago. Over the past month, the estimate has changed +0.3%.

Having a strong externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool, the Zacks Rank, offers a more conclusive picture of a stock's price direction in the near term, since it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions. Due to the size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, IBM is rated Zacks Rank #3 (Hold).

Defensive income gets valuable when growth gets shaky, and this month's list sticks to businesses people pay for in any economy: prescription drugs, enterprise software, breakfast cereal, and electricity. The shared hook is coverage. Each name below pays a dividend that earnings or free cash flow can support, and the group's top yielder, General Mills (NYSE:GIS), now pays a forward yield of 6.74% after the stock fell 16.84% year to date. Every pick prioritizes safety. Yield comes second.

CHIEW / Shutterstock.com
Johnson & Johnson: A Dividend King Guiding Past $100 Billion

Johnson & Johnson (NYSE:JNJ) pays $1.34 per quarter, or $5.36 annualized, for a forward yield of 1.95% at a share price near $274.54. That is the lowest yield on this list, and it reflects a stock that has gained 34.8% this year. J&J earns its spot on safety.

Dividend safety: The board raised the payout 3.1% in April 2026, which the company marked as its 64th consecutive year of increases (a streak that puts it in rare company, the same 50-plus-year club we ranked by valuation in a free Dividend Kings report). The payment history backs that up, with the quarterly rate climbing every year from $0.90 in 2019 to today's $1.34. Against the midpoint of 2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $11.60 to $11.75, the annual dividend uses roughly 46% of earnings, leaving plenty of room for raise number 65.
